items.title: Build an IP set and check the capacity of a rule
items.kills: "A network ACL is the place to block a long list of attacking IP addresses."
items.cost: $0. The task creates no web ACL. AWS WAF charges are based on the number of web ACLs, the rules per web ACL and the web requests received.
items.cost_if_forgotten: $0 a day. An IP set that no web ACL uses adds no charge.
items.read_only_alternative: Use this when you cannot create AWS WAF resources. It changes nothing. Run step 1. List the IP sets of the Region with aws wafv2 list-ip-sets --scope REGIONAL. If a set exists, read its ranges with aws wafv2 get-ip-set --name <NAME> --scope REGIONAL --id <ID> --query "IPSet.Addresses". Then find the --addresses option on the create-ip-set page of the AWS CLI Command Reference and read which CIDR range AWS WAF does not support.

steps.text: Open AWS CloudShell. Read the default quota for rules in one network ACL. You compare it with an IP set later.
steps.expect: The quota name, Rules per network ACL, and its default value. Note the number.

steps.text: Create an IP set for regional resources, such as an Application Load Balancer. It holds one documentation range, 192.0.2.0/24. Keep its ID.
steps.command: aws wafv2 create-ip-set --name saa-edge-protection-t01 --scope REGIONAL --ip-address-version IPV4 --addresses 192.0.2.0/24 --tags Key=book,Value=saa Key=task,Value=edge-protection-t01
steps.expect: No output. IPSET_ID now holds the ID of the new IP set.

steps.text: Read the ARN of the set. A rule refers to the set by this ARN.
steps.expect: No output. IPSET_ARN now holds the ARN of the set.

steps.text: Ask AWS WAF how many web ACL capacity units (WCUs) one Block rule that uses the whole set needs. The check creates no rule and no web ACL. The quotes around $IPSET_ARN let the shell insert the ARN.
steps.expect: Capacity and one number: the WCUs of this one rule.

steps.text: Get the current lock token of the set. AWS WAF asks for this token on every update and delete.
steps.expect: No output. LOCK_TOKEN now holds the token.

steps.text: Try to replace the list with 0.0.0.0/0, which covers every IPv4 address.
steps.expect: An error that rejects the address. The set keeps 192.0.2.0/24.
steps.predict: You want one IP set that blocks every IPv4 address. Will AWS WAF accept the range 0.0.0.0/0?
steps.explain: AWS WAF [supports all IPv4 and IPv6 CIDR ranges except for /0](../facts/waf.md#waf-ip-set-cidr-ipv4-ipv6-not-slash-0), so the update fails and the set keeps its old range. An IP set is for a list of attackers. One set holds [10,000](../facts/waf.md#waf-ip-set-max-addresses) addresses or ranges at most, and a network ACL has [20 rules per network ACL](../facts/vpc.md#vpc-quota-rules-per-network-acl) by default.

steps.text: Fix it: list the attacker ranges themselves. An update replaces the whole list, so name every range. This command uses three documentation ranges and the same lock token.
steps.expect: No output. NEXT_TOKEN now holds the new lock token. The cleanup uses it.

steps.text: Read the addresses in the set.

cleanup.text: Delete the IP set with the newest lock token. If AWS answers WAFOptimisticLockException, run step 5 again, then run this command with $LOCK_TOKEN in place of $NEXT_TOKEN.

verify.expect: An error: AWS WAF cannot find the IP set. If the set still shows, wait one minute and run the command again.

still_costs: Nothing: this task creates no web ACL, and AWS WAF charges are based on web ACLs, rules per web ACL and web requests. Delete the IP set anyway, so that no unused set stays in the account.
If the CloudShell session ended before the cleanup, the variables are empty. Find the ID and the lock token again with aws wafv2 list-ip-sets --scope REGIONAL.
